original_question:
For 0 < b < 1, define ψ_b ∈ L2(R) by ψ̂_b = 1_{(−1,−b)∪(b,1)}.

A frame wavelet is a function ψ whose dyadic wavelet system {ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k)} is a frame for L2(R) with bounds 0 < c ≤ d < ∞.

For what values of 1/8 < b ≤ 1/6 is ψ_b a frame wavelet?
target_in_paper: Section 2.7, Problem 2.7: determine exactly which b in 1/8 < b <= 1/6 make the band-limited function ψ_b, defined by ψ̂_b = 1_{(-1,-b)∪(b,1)}, a dyadic frame wavelet. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target almost exactly: it uses the same family ψ_b, the same unresolved interval 1/8 < b <= 1/6, and the same dyadic frame property for the system {ψ_{j,k}} in L^2(ℝ). It also correctly states the frame inequalities and keeps the scope one-dimensional and dyadic, which is exactly the scope of Problem 2.7. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's dyadic wavelet system is the one from Definition 2.1: ψ_{j,k}(x) = 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x - k) with j, k in ℤ.
To make the question fully stand-alone, the Fourier transform convention used in the paper should be stated explicitly: ψ̂(ξ) = ∫_ℝ ψ(x)e^{-2πixξ} dx.
The paper uses the synonym 'framelet' for 'frame wavelet'; including that terminology would make the rewrite closer to the official wording.
The paper notes that this interval is singled out because the status of ψ_b is already known for all other b in (0,1), via the classification table immediately following Problem 2.7.
refined_question: Using the Fourier transform convention ψ̂(ξ) = ∫_ℝ ψ(x)e^{-2πixξ} dx, let 0 < b < 1 and define ψ_b ∈ L^2(ℝ) by ψ̂_b = 1_{(-1,-b)∪(b,1)}. For j, k ∈ ℤ, set ψ_{b;j,k}(x) = 2^{j/2} ψ_b(2^j x - k). Determine exactly those parameters b ∈ (1/8, 1/6] for which the dyadic wavelet system {ψ_{b;j,k} : j, k ∈ ℤ} is a frame for L^2(ℝ); equivalently, for which there exist constants 0 < c ≤ d < ∞ such that c||f||_2^2 ≤ Σ_{j,k∈ℤ} |⟨f, ψ_{b;j,k}⟩|^2 ≤ d||f||_2^2 for every f ∈ L^2(ℝ).
justification: This is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of the paper's official open problem in Section 2.7. The only refinements needed are to import the dyadic-system notation from Definition 2.1, the frame inequalities from the paper's definition of a framelet, and the Fourier transform convention stated earlier in Section 2. The surrounding context on page 6 also explains that (1/8, 1/6] is the remaining unresolved parameter range, with all other b already classified in the table following Problem 2.7. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
